thread:
maria_cs: Quick heads-up — AtlasAI onboarding. They reported 95th pct latency spikes on long prompts (~>512 tokens) yesterday during their nightly batch tests. Renewal conversation in 3 weeks; they're sensitive to tail latency. :eyes:

maria_cs: Metrics: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~1.6s, cost drift up ~18% month-over-month. They called out hallucinations in some rerank flows but main ask is 'make responses faster and cheaper'.

tyler_eng: timeline + details? do we have traces or example requests?

maria_cs: Sent a sample request in #support-ticket-452 — but quick excerpt (from their internal load test):
```
REQ id=afe21 prompt_len=780 model=redwood-rlhf-large max_tokens=1024
SERVING node=dedicated-3 kernel=fused-attn kv_hits=42 kv_misses=18 latency=1600ms
```

anika_ml: looks like large prompts are causing kernel fallback + KV cache churn. two quick levers: 1) quantized int8 variant for batch inference (saves GPU memory & often better throughput for long sequences) 2) routing by sequence-length: short prompts -> faster fp16 replica, long prompts -> quantized large-context node with more cache memory.

leo_pm: good. Maria — customer sentiment? are they willing to trial a performance pilot or do we need to ship a proposal to their procurement first?

maria_cs: They're open to a pilot but want clear SLOs. Biggest worry: we change quality with quantization and then hallucinations increase. They asked we keep regen rate <= current baseline and show cost delta.

anika_ml: understood. Proposal: Canary plan — route 20% of traffic (by user-id hashing) to int8-q model variant behind a canary policy, enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, and set automatic fallback to fp16 if generation-quality regression detected via our eval hooks. Measure token-cost, median latency, p95, and regen-rate over 48h.

tyler_eng: implementation notes: can implement a routing rule in Redwood Console: route.if(hash(user_id)%100 < 20 && seq_len > 256) -> model:rlhf-large-int8-canary, else -> rlhf-large-fp16. Also enable cache.ttl=3600 for their onboarding prompts. I can drop the routing policy and rollout in dev tomorrow.

leo_pm: capture acceptance criteria for the customer: 1) p95 reduced by >=30% for long prompts OR cost/token reduced by >=25% without regen-rate > baseline +2%. 2) No customer-visible errors for 48h. Would trigger larger rollout.

maria_cs: I'll propose that in the next renewal prep call and ask for permission to run 48h pilot. I also want an enablement checklist we can send: how to interpret metrics, how to opt-out of canary per-user, and rollback steps.

anika_ml: I'll draft the tech runbook and eval hooks (quality regression detectors tied to their prompt set). Example eval config:
```
- seed_prompts: 250
- metrics: exact_match_rate, regen_rate, bert_score
- rollback_thresholds: regen_rate +2%, bert_score drop 0.03
```

tyler_eng: infra-bot: deploy routing policy and canary config to staging for verification.

infra-bot: deploy request accepted — job 6221 queued. staging rollout ETA ~ 45m. :rocket:

maria_cs: action items: Maria -> schedule pilot kickoff with AtlasAI and legal (by EOD), Tyler -> staging canary + dashboard (tomorrow), Anika -> runbook + eval hooks (48h), Leo -> update renewal talking points with pilot offer.

leo_pm: I'll also add a slide showing projected monthly cost delta and expected SLA improvement for renewal pack.

maria_cs: capturing customer feedback plan: we'll run a short 10-question NPS-style check after 48h and a qualitative interview if they opt in. If they report quality regressions, we will automatically shrink canary to 0% and trigger a postmortem.

tyler_eng: one more technical caveat — quantized models sometimes underperform on very long context due to dequantization overhead; we'll keep a fallback policy on sequence > 2048 to route to fp16.

anika_ml: thanks — I'll add that to runbook.

maria_cs: Thanks team — I'll update AtlasAI and book kickoff for Monday. :pray:
